translationRepairs: Combine this result with the hourly mean moon-sun elongation: if both equations call for addition, add the larger second equation and subtract the smaller; if both call for subtraction, subtract the larger and add the smaller.
Combine this result with the hourly mean moon-sun elongation: if both equations call for addition, add when the second equation is larger and subtract when it is smaller.

s0090 only states the both-add case (兩均同加，後均大則加，小則減); the both-subtract rule is the separate next sentence s0091. The before invents that same-sign subtraction case here; the proposed after keeps only the both-add rule and matches 後均大則加，小則減.

To find apparent-time moon distance from limit: subtract sun ecliptic longitude from apparent-time ecliptic-horizon quadrant mansion degree, remainder is moon distance from limit; follow whether limit is east or west.

To find apparent-time moon distance from limit: subtract apparent-time ecliptic-horizon quadrant mansion degree from sun ecliptic longitude, remainder is moon distance from limit; follow whether limit is east or west.

s0244 treats sun ecliptic longitude greater than the quadrant mansion as limit-east, so the remainder is sun minus quadrant; the literal before reverses that subtraction. The proposal’s order is right, but it drops 求用時月距限 (“To find…”) and starts with an unsupported “Then,” so restore the framing while correcting the operands.
Beyond forty-five degrees, first contact is to the upper right and last contact to the lower left.
Beyond forty-five degrees, first contact is rightward with an upward bias, and last contact leftward with a downward bias.

s0388 has 初虧右偏上，復圓左偏下, with right/left primary and up/down as bias; s0387’s 上偏右/下偏左 is the reverse hierarchy. Rendering both as “upper right/lower left” erases that distinction; “rightward with an upward bias” / “leftward with a downward bias” restores it.
Past ninety degrees, first contact is to the lower right and last contact to the upper left.
Past ninety degrees, first contact is rightward with a downward bias, and last contact leftward with an upward bias.
s0390’s 初虧右偏下，復圓左偏上 marks right/left as primary with vertical bias, distinct from 下偏右/上偏左. “To the lower right/upper left” collapses that contrast; the proposed bias phrasing is accurate.
Beyond forty-five degrees, first contact is to the lower right and last contact to the upper left.
Beyond forty-five degrees, first contact is rightward with a downward bias, and last contact leftward with an upward bias.

s0392 again has 右偏下/左偏上 against s0391’s 下偏右/上偏左; using the same “lower right/upper left” wording for both is a real loss of directional hierarchy. The replacement keeps right/left primary with vertical bias.
Past ninety degrees, first contact is to the upper right and last contact to the lower left.
Past ninety degrees, first contact is rightward with an upward bias, and last contact leftward with a downward bias.
s0394’s 初虧右偏上，復圓左偏下 is the right/left-primary form, not the same as 上偏右/下偏左. The before collapses them; “rightward with an upward bias” / “leftward with a downward bias” matches the Chinese.
